R7BB-bear-backcountry-0001.name: 920 m NW of Cypress Creek
R7BB-bear-backcountry-0001.pressureWhy: More than 5 km from a drivable road (estimate).
R7BB-bear-backcountry-0001.parkWhat: pull off on an unnamed gravel road

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2006 (20 years old), 490 m N: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
SE facing slope, 15 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Unnamed wetland 50 m S: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from District of Hudsons Hope, about 150 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate). Via Beryl Prairie Rd, unsigned, Beryl Prairie FSR, Haystack FSR.
Park: 56.92675, -122.93568, pull off on an unnamed gravel road. Map links below.
Walk: 5.7 km SW, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 287 m, about 142 min at 3 km/h.
Camp: flat ground 100 m E of the spot at 1,158 m (56.89391, -123.00497). Water: unnamed wetland 120 m SW (estimate).

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Aug, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 7-57, Region 7B. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-05, closures 2026-10-16.
